get.description:
Retrieves NASA FIRMS wildfire detection data within the specified bounding box.
      Data includes MODIS NRT fire detections with confidence values and fire radiative power.

      Features:
      - Fire location, carried by geometry.coordinates as [longitude, latitude]
      - Raw confidence value from the FIRMS feed, which each client buckets itself
      - Optional minimum confidence filtering in the database query
      - Fire Radiative Power (FRP) in megawatts, null when the feed omitted it

      The acquisition date, acquisition time and satellite are no longer returned.

      Data is returned in GeoJSON FeatureCollection format for easy mapping.
      Feature order is not part of the contract, clustered or not. Sort client-side if
      you need one; the API takes no view on confidence and so cannot order by it.

      A cluster carries its count and the zoom it splits at, and nothing else. It is
      not summarised by confidence, FRP or recency: read those from the individual
      detections a cluster resolves to when you zoom in.

      Clustering:
      - Pass 'zoom' to receive dense areas aggregated into clusters. Omit it and every
        detection is returned individually, which is what clients built before
        clustering do. Note that only the aggregation is opt-in: the trimmed property
        set above applies to every response, clustered or not.
      - Clusters are selected by their centre. A cluster whose centre falls just
        outside the requested bbox is not returned, even when some of its detections
        are inside it. This matches how the sensor layer answers a viewport; padding
        the lookup was tried and does not fix it, because a detection can sit further
        from its cluster's centre than any fixed pad.
      - A returned cluster can still aggregate detections from just outside the bbox,
        because the underlying query is widened by a fixed buffer for edge coverage.
        'fireCount' is therefore not a count of what is strictly in view.
      - A clustered response is a mix. A feature carrying 'fireCount' is a cluster; a
        feature without it is a single detection and still carries confidence and frp.
        An isolated detection is never wrapped in a cluster of one.
      - A cluster also carries 'expansionZoom', the zoom at which it breaks into its
        children. Move the map there when the user taps it and the cluster is
        guaranteed to split; guessing a zoom step instead can land short and leave the
        same cluster on screen.
      - Above the clustering gate the response is individual detections regardless.
      - 'count' remains the number of detections, so on a clustered response it is
        larger than features.length.

info.title: AirGradient Map API
info.description:
**AirGradient Map API** - Access real-time and historical air quality data from the global AirGradient monitoring network.

AirGradient publishes measurements from AirGradient monitors and third-party data owners. Datasource, owner, provider, and location license metadata explain attribution and reuse context. Keep those fields visible when displaying or redistributing API data.

Some datasources are available only inside AirGradient products under provider agreements and are not exposed through the public API. Public API availability does not grant reuse rights. Users remain responsible for following datasource owner terms and any licenses attached to each location.

If a location has no listed license, no explicit license has been stored for that location. It does not mean the data is unrestricted.

Clustering is computed per request from the detections this viewport returned, so a group near the edge is built from a truncated set: its fireCount can change as the user pans. Treat a cluster count as a property of the current view, not of the area.
